deep.reconstruction:
Problem: find the critical (buckling) load P of a column of height AC = a whose flexural rigidity varies as K(x) = Ekk·s^{4λ}, with s = α + βx/a. This covers geometrically similar cross-sections whose linear size grows like s^λ.

Bending equation: K(x)y'' + Py = 0. With ds = (β/a)dx and P = n²β²Ekk/a², it becomes s^{4λ} y_ss + n² y = 0. In modern terms this is a Bessel equation: y = √s·Z_ν(n s^{1−2λ}/(1−2λ)) with ν = 1/(2(1−2λ)).

On the previous page Euler gives a series solution y = b√(R²+Q²)·sin(ζ + n/v − Φ). Here v = (2λ−1)s^{2λ−1}, tan Φ = Q/R, and R, Q are series in 1/n. The coefficients 𝔄, 𝔅, … make the series terminate exactly when ν is a half-integer. The buckling condition takes the phase from 0 at s = α to π at s = α+β, and then P = n²β²Ekk/a².

This page:
(i) λ = 0 (uniform column): the condition gives −nβ = π, so P = π²Ekk/a², the classical Euler load.
(ii) Example 1, λ = 1 (rigidity ∝ (α+βx/a)⁴, e.g. a truncated cone or pyramid): v = s, R = s, Q = 0, so y = b·s·sin(ζ + n/s). This is the exact elementary solution of s⁴y'' + n²y = 0 (ν = −1/2). The conditions ζ = −n/α and −n/α + n/(α+β) = π give nβ = −πα(α+β). Hence P = π²α²(α+β)²Ekk/a², the exact critical load of the conical column, matching his earlier direct treatment.
(iii) Example 2, λ = 1/3 (rigidity ∝ s^{4/3}, ν = 3/2): v = −1/(3s^{1/3}), 𝔄 = 1/3, 𝔅 = 0, so R = s^{1/3}, Q = 1/(3n), tan Φ = 1/(3n s^{1/3}). This is the spherical-Bessel (j₁/y₁) closed form with argument t = 3n s^{1/3}: amplitude ∝ s^{1/3}√(1+1/t²), phase t + arctan(1/t). The next page turns this into a transcendental eigenvalue equation and solves it by perturbation for small β.
errors: In the λ = 1 example the expression 'π = −nb/(α(α+β))' should read −nβ/(α(α+β)); the 'b' is a misprint or misreading for β. The next line, nβ = −πα(α+β), and the resulting P are correct.
Sign convention: n comes out negative (−nβ = π). This is harmless because only n² enters P.

Not on this page but in the continuation: 'A tg 2/(3n∛(α+β))' should have 1 in the numerator. 'P = nnβ/aa·Ekk' should be nnββ. The intermediate approximation −nβ = π + ββ/(9π) is inconsistent with the final first-order result P ≈ π²(1+2β/3)Ekk/a², which is the correct one (mean rigidity).

ideas.what: Critical load of a uniform pinned column, P = π²EI/a², recovered as the λ = 0 case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 Methodus inveniendi, Additamentum I; 1757/59 papers)

ideas.what: Exact buckling load of a column with rigidity ∝ (α+βx/a)⁴, via the solution y = s·sin(c + n/s)
ideas.modern_name: Exact buckling of a tapered (conical/pyramidal) column; elementary Bessel case ν = −1/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (later systematized by Dinnik and others for tapered columns)
ideas.where_published: E238 earlier sections; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Rigidity ∝ s^{4/3} gives a closed-form solution with sin and arctan (amplitude √(s^{2/3}+1/(9n²)))
ideas.modern_name: Half-integer-order Bessel (spherical Bessel j₁/y₁) closed form; integrable cases of the Riccati-type equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli / Riccati (integrability conditions); Euler; later Bessel, Lommel
ideas.where_published: E238; Euler's Riccati-equation papers; Truesdell's commentary

ideas.what: Buckling condition as a phase-advance condition: phase increases by π between the ends
ideas.modern_name: Prüfer-type phase / WKB-like amplitude–phase representation of a Sturm–Liouville eigenvalue problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Prüfer (1926) for the phase method; Sturm–Liouville (1836)

deep.surprise_reason: The page works out known special cases (uniform column, conical column, the s^{4/3} case) of Euler's tapered-column analysis. These are already covered in Truesdell's commentary on Euler's elasticity work. The amplitude–phase formulation is an early analogue of Prüfer/WKB methods, but this is recognized in the historical literature on E238.
transcription_corrections: '−\frac{nb}{\alpha(\alpha+\beta)}' should be '−\frac{n\beta}{\alpha(\alpha+\beta)}'. The printed glyph is likely β, or else it is a misprint.
'v = −\frac{1}{3}s^{-\frac{1}{3}}' matches the image; the printed form is '−⅓ s^{−⅓} = −1/(3∛s)'.
